segments.text: You are going to listen to a conversation between a state agent and a student who wants to rent a room.
First, you have some time to look at questions 1 to 10.
Now listen carefully and answer questions 1 to 10.
AZ Holmes, Sophie Bryan speaking. How can I help you?
Oh, hi. I'm moving to Bristol to start university there this autumn.
I'm looking for a room to rent, probably for the full three years of my course.
Right, I see. Well, let's get your details.
Yes, my name is Harley Elliot. That's H-A-R-L-E-Y, Harley, and E-double-L-I-O-double-T-E, Elliot.
Okay Harley, and can I have your phone number, the best number to get you on?
Well, that's definitely not my home number because I'm often out.
So here's my mobile number, 0784371 5711.
Alright, and an email address please, so we can send you out all the information and forms.
Uh, is it okay if I give you my brother's email?
He works in IT, so he's better at getting emails and printing stuff than me.
That's fine, as long as you complete the forums and send them back to us.
Okay, here it is.
Andy at globaltech.com.
Andy is his name, and then global, and tech from technology, you know?
Certainly.
About occupation, I will put down student. Is that correct?
Yes, I'll be studying an undergraduate course at UWE for the next few years.
Right. Now, what kind of accommodation are you looking for? House, apartment or a studio?
Which one is the cheapest? Not the studio, I believe.
Definitely not. And an apartment generally costs more than a house.
You can share a house with two or three other people.
I will choose the cheapest option. I only need a single room since I don't
spend much time in my room anyway, but it must be fully furnished. I don't
want to go shopping for furniture. Alright, I'll put that down.
What else do you need? How about kitchen equipment?
Do you have any special requirements? Well, I can only cook simple dishes,
So a cooker in a fridge to store fresh produce is good enough. A dishwasher would be nice in
case I don't feel like doing the dishes but it's not a must. Neither is a microwave or a toaster
to be honest. I'll make a note of that. Now about location, have you done any research
into the Bristol area? Not too much actually. Well you love going out right? The city centre
might be suitable for you because it has a big shopping area named Cabot Circus
along with numerous bars and restaurants. That sounds great but I reckon it will be a
little expensive. Oh yeah, let me check that. The lowest price for a room in
the centre is £450, bills included. What's your budget for accommodation?
Hmm, well I'd like to spend about £300. The best I can do is £350.
Okay, then I recommend the Filton area. It's fairly close to your university, and if you want to spend time in the centre, you can always take the bus. They run until midnight.
Yeah, that doesn't sound too bad actually. Hmm, I think I'll live near the university. Anyway, I am coming to Bristol to study, not to party.
Alright, any request for the location? Would you like to be near a supermarket?
Not really, I can always order things online, but I'd prefer a bus stop nearby.
One final question, do you smoke or have any pets?
I smoke sometimes, but I don't have any pets.
Okay, warm is finished. We will send a list of suitable properties for you to choose from via email.
Can I ask, how did you hear about us? Newspaper, website or TV?
I just googled it on the internet, you know. Your agency popped up first on the list.
Ah, that's right. Thank you for calling us.
